function: Joint communication and sensing precoding for multi-static ISAC with full-duplex cell-free APs: unsupervised JcsNet outputs precoders maximizing sum rate under a sensing SINR constraint (p. 9-10).
system: Cell-free full-duplex ISAC: 10 APs with 4 antennas, 4 UL and 4 DL single-antenna UEs, one target; no RIS; frequency not stated (p. 11).
method: Unsupervised JcsNet (spatial attention, 4 residual CNN blocks, power projection, learned safety margin); loss is negative sum rate plus sensing-constraint penalty; offline training, online execution (p. 10-12).
data_channel: Own simulator, 100 m circle: Rayleigh communication channels, LoS sensing channel; 10000 training and 1000 test channels; cluster-based ISAC model [41] used only to validate it (p. 11-13).
test_conditions: Trained on 10000 channels (target present or absent) of one scene; tested on 1000 held-out channels of that scene; a network trained per sensing threshold (p. 12-13).
baselines: Non-learned only: MRT and ZF communication with conjugate sensing precoding (rho_com 0.5, 0.8), and joint SDP-based precoding J-SDP [37]; no learned baseline (p. 12).
metrics: UL/DL sum rate (SE), sensing rate log2(1+SINR), sensing-constraint violation rate, detection probabilities; CDFs over 200 random scenarios (p. 11-13).
complexity: none (only a qualitative claim of competitive execution speed, p. 11; Table II lists layer structure only, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 11: "the communication channel is modeled with Rayleigh fading, and the sensing channel is modeled with LoS paths"; the 3GPP-derived cluster-based model [41] is used only "to compare the cluster-based channel model with our idealized channel model", not for training or testing.
q2_support: p. 13: "as the test set to verify the efficacy of the trained JcsNet"; p. 12: "in the scene are generated to train the JcsNet"; the test channels come from the same scene and no different scenario, band or configuration is reported.
q3_support: p. 12: "JSC precoding based on semi-definite programming (J-SDP) [37]" is the joint design benchmark, the other two are MRT and ZF with conjugate sensing precoding; all are non-learned and no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "enabling competitive execution speeds compared to traditional methods [27]" is a qualitative statement; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime is reported (Table II, p. 12, lists only the layer structure).
q5_support: p. 12: "in the scene are generated to train the JcsNet" shows simulated data only; the paper gives no link or DOI to code or data and uses no public or measured dataset.
notes: Included, area 5: only stage four (JcsNet) is learned, stages one to three (MMSE estimation, MAPRT detector) are classical. The cluster-based ISAC model [41] derives sensing channels from the 3GPP model but serves only to validate the idealized Rayleigh/LoS model (p. 11), so q1 is 0. Fig. 10 uses 200 randomly generated scenarios (p. 13) without saying they differ from the training scene, so q2 is 0; the reviewer may confirm. Table II was read from the page image (p. 12).
